verdict: PASS within the reviewed recovery-artifact component scope; no unresolved blocking findings.
independence: Reviewer authored only external receipts and ephemeral-copy regression fixtures. No production recovery component was authored or edited by this reviewer. Root independently reviews the separate reviewer-authored ingestion seam.
checks: Unchanged isolated helper, static SQLite preparation, format and strict all-target Clippy passed on the unmodified checkpoint.

19 focused recovery unit cases passed, including two independent cases, actual SIGKILL at created/staged/renamed private checkpoints, and real 1 MiB private filesystem ENOSPC. One explicit source-fault-only case was ignored in normal execution and run separately with its fault.
Eight authored public recovery tests and the unchanged independent retained-log regression passed; repeated restored source unit and eight public cases passed.
All four deliberate guard/progress regressions compiled and failed at runtime with the expected assertions; none was classified solely from compilation failure.

resolved_findings.finding: Long-lived regular descriptors retained deleted log/spool bytes outside directory budgets and could outlive owner locking.
resolved_findings.evidence: retained-log-initial.json: actual RED 4,194,376 bytes against 4,194,304 cap. Unchanged fixture on corrected source reports 3,145,800 named, zero detached, PASS.
resolved_findings.resolution: Opaque stat-identity tokens retain shared ownership authority, not regular file descriptors. Per-operation reads close before unlink/rotation; held tokens retain the lock and cannot authorize another instance.

resolved_findings.finding: Bounded replay selected random EventId order before predecessor sequence.
resolved_findings.resolution: Generated names sort fixed-width scoped sequence before EventId; decoded record must match named sequence. Actual 64-record adversarial UUID-order test returns 1..32. Independent sequence-tamper test passes; deleting comparison causes runtime RED.

resolved_findings.finding: Successful unlink followed by directory fsync failure lost actual partial progress.
resolved_findings.resolution: Increment removed files/bytes and discarded artifacts immediately after successful unlink, before fsync; preserve failure and unknown gap. Explicit source-level post-unlink fsync fault passes actual progress; moving counts after the same fault fails 0 vs 1. This fault is injected in a private source copy, not a real kernel fsync failure.

resolved_findings.finding: A single dropped count could falsely mix rejected attempts, artifacts and unique lost events.
resolved_findings.resolution: rejected_attempts and discarded_artifacts are separate saturating volatile quantities; unknown_gap remains explicit. Neither is a durable unique-event-loss total.

security_disposition: Public production reviewed mapping registry remains empty. Real and handcrafted synthetic public inputs fail closed. Source-specific strings cannot qualify themselves; private cfg(test) synthetic mappings exercise the same prewrite and replay gates.

Removing the required-turn source guard persists one artifact before replay rejects; the before-temp canary test detects this at runtime (1 vs 0). Removing the replay eligibility guard independently admits a previously staged event under an unproven mapping and is detected.

Fixed descriptor-relative private directory and filenames, local-filesystem allowlist, lock authority, nofollow/type/mode/UID/link checks and full stat identities guard reads and bounded cleanup. Unknown names remain protected while consuming global inventory budget.

Temporary, partial, ready, old-generation and orphan file bytes consume bounded accounting. Expiry stops replay at the approved artifact TTL; removal still requires explicit bounded preview/apply. Original event identity/generation remain intact.
Only fixed codes and numeric manager data enter logs/status; no caller-provided source text, path or OS error string is formatted there.

maintainability.disposition: Accept write_stage 52 lexical nonblank lines: one contiguous create, bounded write, file/directory sync, identity validation, no-replace publish and receipt lifecycle, including private crash checkpoints. Keeping descriptor/token lifetimes and durability ordering together is clearer than a metric-only split. No recovery file exceeds 300 nonblank lines.

limits: This component review does not independently qualify the complete integrated reducer/coordinator/storage branch, hosted Docker checks or mandatory native qualification.
All production adapters remain unsupported in M1 until independently reviewed version-specific source mappings exist; private synthetic success is not live harness evidence.
Bounds cover file-content byte lengths and finite file/handle inventories; they do not assert exact filesystem allocation including block/metadata overhead or isolate hostile same-UID code.
Cleanup is nonrecursive and partial-progress-aware, not transactionally atomic across files. Loss accounting is volatile and deliberately retains unknown gap.

The first reviewer execution repeated a fixed-name independent fixture in the same private state and received AlreadyExists. That fixture reuse error is preserved under attempt-1 and is not a product failure; a fresh run completed all expected checks.
